note: KNOWN critical/serious axe violations, keyed story|theme|rule. The build fails on any fingerprint NOT listed here (a new violation). Grow-only via `pnpm --filter @adminium/ui a11y --update-baseline`; remove a fixed entry by deleting its line. Harness errors are never listed. See scripts/a11y-sweep.mjs.
howToMeasure: Run it where the harness WAITS FOR THE STORY. scripts/a11y-sweep.mjs navigates with networkidle and .storybook/preview.tsx stamps data-vrt-ready on DOM quiescence; before both, the flag went up on mount while each widget family's lazily-imported body was still in flight, so the sweep scanned empty widget frames. This file is NOT platform-specific — an earlier revision of this note said it was, and that was wrong.

2026-08-18.whatTheNumbersDid: 162 -> 112. Three claims were made about this before the cause was understood, and the first two were wrong: 162 -> 1 (measured on a fast laptop that lost a race), then 162 -> 111 called LINUX-CANONICAL (measured on CI, which won the same race). The machines were never disagreeing about accessibility.
2026-08-18.theRace: data-vrt-ready was a bare mount effect. The widget registry loads component code through the definitions lazy refs, one Vite chunk per family, so the flag rose while the bodies were still loading. Measured on widgets-forms--light-ltr: 101 elements at the flag, 182 three seconds later. On widgets-tables-trackf--master-list-story: 30 vs 124. Whichever side of that a machine landed on decided its result, which also makes this the likeliest cause of the intermittent widget-render failures this repo has been re-running past.
2026-08-18.harnessDefect1: src/styles/storybook.css @source-d only packages/ui, while .storybook/main.ts has loaded the widgets and charts stories since 04-T17. Tailwind v4 generates utilities from source TEXT, so every widget and chart story rendered with class attributes and no rules behind them.
2026-08-18.harnessDefect2: Nothing painted --bg/--fg on the preview body, so Storybook white showed through and dark-theme foregrounds were measured against it. axe resolves color-contrast against the nearest opaque ancestor, so the translucent tone tints composited over white and reported pairs the product never renders.
2026-08-18.reconciliation: Against the original 162: 111 do not reproduce and were artifacts of the two defects above; 51 were real all along; 59 more were exposed once the stories rendered styled. 128 violations were found and FIXED rather than baselined - alpha-dimmed small text, six keyboard-unreachable scroll regions, role=row containers with no cell children, a dl with a p child, an aria-expanded row that should have been a button, and two dimmed surfaces that never said aria-disabled.
2026-08-18.stillOpen: 112 entries, dominated by scrollable-region-focusable, color-contrast and nested-interactive. None individually accepted yet; RELEASE-GATE.md keeps that row unchecked.

history.2026-08-19: 112 -> 69. A BURN-DOWN, not a re-measurement — the distinction the 2026-08-18 entry above failed to make. Every one of these 43 was removed because component code changed, and each was verified gone by re-running the sweep against a freshly built Storybook rather than by editing this file. 20 nested-interactive: DocumentCanvas wrapped every block in `role="button" tabIndex={0}`, which is children-presentational — the line-item table, its column headers and its inputs were stripped from the accessibility tree and the whole block announced as one flat string. The wrapper is now inert and selection rides a real <button> named from the block's own localized heading. 12 aria-valid-attr-value: TabBar renders no TabsContent by design, but Radix's Trigger emits `aria-controls` at a panel id unconditionally, so every selected tab pointed at an element never in the DOM (axe skips the dangling IDREF on unselected triggers, which is why it was 12 and not 60). 11 color-contrast: three wrapper opacity utilities that dragged informational text beside operable controls to 2.2-3.3:1 (OpsApi 4, OpsTrust 2, ConnectionStatus 1), and the loyalty banner moved off the accent tint where its headline number measured 4.42:1 (4). NOT pruned, deliberately: the two qa-widget-states--tables-states entries did not reproduce BEFORE this change either, so there is no evidence they are fixed rather than below axe's 13px overflow buffer on this machine. Removing an entry you have not fixed is how a baseline stops meaning anything. LATER THE SAME DAY, 69 -> 53: the gantt canvas's 16 `scrollable-region-focusable` entries, cleared by removing the overflow rather than by making the region focusable. The timeline was never clipped — at the sweep's own viewport the canvas measured 746 against 734 — the 12px came from one absolutely-positioned milestone diamond sitting at ~100%. Adding tabIndex would have put a keyboard stop on a region with nothing in it to reach, which is a usability regression that happens to satisfy axe; clamping the marker removes the phantom scroll instead. The today-line marker is clamped too, or a project dated to the last day reintroduces it. AND 53 -> 49: ScheduleMatrix's 4 `aria-required-children`. Its role="table" rows had a bare <span> in column 1 and undecorated coverage cells, so rows were missing the header/cell roles the role requires — column 1 announced as nothing. Ported verbatim from the already-correct twin, ShiftMatrix, and the twin got the two bits IT was missing (columnheader on its own leading span, aria-hidden on its Avatar) so the fork stops drifting. The Avatar needed hiding either way or the rowheader's name doubled to "Ana Trujillo Ana Trujillo, Manager · 32h". AND 49 -> 29: the 20 remaining `scrollable-region-focusable` in DiagnosticsReadout and ValidationIssuesList. Unlike the gantt these DO clip content, so they earn a tab stop — but a CONDITIONAL one. `useScrollRegion` measures and attaches `tabIndex`/`role` only while the container actually overflows, so a resize that removes the clipping removes the stop. No `+13` fudge against axe's buffer: axe fired on the gantt at 12px, so mirroring 13 would leave a flagged node without a stop. The region is named by the WidgetFrame heading id (new WidgetHeadingContext) rather than an invented string — so it announces the words on screen and adds ZERO i18n keys, which matters because the previous aria-label batch shipped as literal English into seven locales. The list passes no role: an explicit one would override the <ul>'s implicit role=list and destroy the 'list, N items' count. Still NOT pruned: the two qa-widget-states entries, unexplained for the fourth pass running — TopMoversList overflows by 6px from a fixed-width delta column, which is a layout defect to fix rather than a region to make focusable. AND 29 -> 25: MasterList's 4 `nested-interactive`, the last of that rule. The row carried role="button" + tabIndex + a key handler, which made every descendant presentational — a screen-reader user heard one flattened string and lost the StatusPill, the ProgressBar's value and the Switch's role and on/off state. The row is now inert and selection rides the visible TITLE as a real button whose ::after stretches the hit area back over the whole row, so the mouse target and the focus ring are unchanged and no sr-only duplicate or new i18n key is needed. The Switch gets `relative z-10` to sit above that hit area, and loses a stopPropagation that had nothing left to stop. track-f-widgets.test.tsx passed UNCHANGED, which is the tell that the visible title really is the control now. AND 25 -> 9: the contrast pass. 16 gantt `color-contrast` closed by giving the progress-% label an OPAQUE plate — the label was painted `--fg-muted`, a token sized for the grey TRACK, while sitting on the solid tone FILL, and the `pct > 55` ternary was a percentage proxy for a pixel question that was wrong at most bar widths. Composited from the token CSS: worst case 1.01:1 (dark --pos) to 8.75:1 light / 9.25:1 dark, now invariant across all 6 tones and all 8 accents because the fill no longer participates. The rest closed by pre-composited `--*-soft-solid` chip tints, so a chip's contrast is a property of the chip rather than of whatever it was re-parented onto; a gradient recipe that reached the same pixel was REJECTED because it converts a measured violation into `incomplete: bgGradient`, removing every chip from axe's reach.

widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.what: A danger status Tag (bg-danger-soft text-danger) inside a SELECTED DataGrid row (bg-accent-soft) in dark theme. Measured 4.41:1 against 4.5:1.
widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.whyNotFixedHere: Both tints are translucent by design, so a tone chip on a selected row composites tone-soft over accent-soft over the surface. Across the dark palette - 8 accents x 4 surfaces x 4 tones - 44 pairs fail, from 4.50 down to 3.54 (black accent, --surface-3, danger). This story is simply the one that renders it.
widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.whatTheGateDoesNotSee: packages/tokens/scripts/contrast-check.mjs measures <tone> on <tone>-soft over each SURFACE and every one passes. It does not measure a soft tint over ANOTHER soft tint, which is what a selected row is.
widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.theDecisionItNeeds: Palette-wide, one of three: lower the dark soft-tint alpha (14% -> 12% clears it at 4.60, visibly changing every tinted chip in dark); make tone-soft opaque, removing the stacking and the adaptability with it; or stop washing selected rows behind chip-bearing cells. Whichever is chosen, the gate should gain the composition.
